exercises.instruction: Complete the sentences with a word from the box.
items: In Britain you have to have a TV (1).......................... and the money from it pays for the BBC. BBC 1 and BBC 2 are (2)............................ channels, but if you have a satellite (3)............................ , you can get satellite TV like Sky. Some people prefer to have (4)............................ TV to satellite.

exercises.instruction: Complete the definitions with a suitable word. The first letter has been given.
items: 1 A TV advertisement shown between programmes: a c............................ .
2 A number of programmes about the same characters which makes people laugh: a c............................ s............................ .
3 A programme which is on TV several times a week and follows the lives of a group of characters: a s............................ o............................ .
4 A programme about a social or political situation which is in the news at the moment: a c............................ a............................ programme.
5 A number of programmes about a group of people in various situations which is intende[?] to be exciting and interesting: a d............................ s............................ .
6 A programme with factual information, sometimes about a place, wildlife, a social problem, etc: a d............................ .
7 A programme in which people have to answer questions or play games to win a prize: a q............................ show.
8 A programme where a presenter talks to famous people about their lives and careers: a c............................ show.

exercises.instruction: Complete the questions in the dialogue below.
items: B: Well, there's an interview with the Prime Minister on BBC 1 and there's a Robert de Niro film on ITV.
B: At 10.30 – after the news.
B: About two hours, I think. Oh, I forgot! There's football on Channel 5 at 7.00 – it's Manchester United versus Barcelona.
B: No, I think it's just the recorded highlights – the match is in the afternoon.

exercises.instruction: Correct the mistake in each sentence.
items: 1 If your television isn't working, perhaps you have forgotten to plug it.
2 Oh, dear, this is such a boring film – look, the news is about to start on the other chann[?] Could you turn down?
3 Turn the TV up, will you – the children are trying to go to sleep.
4 Don't turn the TV on – I'm watching it.
5 The baby loves the TV. She's always trying to switch it down.
